hero.title: See the problem, the proof, and the boundary.
hero.lede: This page separates permissioned client work from LDW-owned systems and internal proof. Each example is bounded to what is live, documented, and deliberately not being claimed.

clientWork.title: Local sites we've rebuilt.
clientWork.lede: Permissioned public examples of live client websites LDW has delivered. Evidence stays bounded to what is live and documented—no unsupported outcome claims.

items.name: East Coast Foam
items.context: A Lowcountry insulation, roofing, and coating contractor needed a clearer, maintainable production site and a controlled path away from the legacy website and infrastructure arrangement.
items.work: Modernized the site structure and content, moved production into the customer-owned GitHub and Cloudflare boundary, preserved mail during the controlled cutover, and added repeatable browser, production-health, validation, and security checks.
items.proof: Current production site with service, recent-work, review, service-area, and estimate/contact journeys.
items.boundary: Customer owns the production repository and infrastructure; LDW provides ongoing managed-site and quality support. No revenue, lead, ranking, or energy-result claim.

items.name: Donovan Family Dentistry
items.context: A Beaufort family dental practice needed a current, easier-to-navigate public site for services, dentists, office information, and patient forms.
items.work: Modernized the public site, organized service and provider content, improved patient-facing navigation, and added responsive/browser, accessibility, performance, security, and release/recovery checks.
items.proof: Current production site with dentist profiles, service/procedure information, office hours/contact/directions, and patient-form access.
items.boundary: Public website work only. No patient-growth, treatment-outcome, HIPAA-certification, compliance-certification, or customer-owned-repository claim.

internalProof.title: Tools we build to make the work clearer.
internalProof.lede: A few current examples show how LDW builds practical tools around real business tasks. They are internal development examples, not products available for purchase.

projects.name: G.A.S. Engine
projects.purpose: Bring website and search findings together so our team can see what changed, where each finding came from, and what deserves a closer look.
projects.description: G.A.S. is LDW's custom-developed SEO research tool. It helps our team review website and search findings over time and explain the evidence behind a next step. It is an internal tool, not software customers can buy or use on their own.
evidence: Provider-neutral typed facts within accepted boundaries
Supports service-first Search + AI Visibility validation
projects.boundary: G.A.S. remains internal infrastructure; customer-facing service claims and pricing remain governed by the separate Managed Search + AI Visibility gate.
projects.whyItMatters: For a small business owner, an SEO report should make it easier to understand what was noticed and why it matters. G.A.S. helps LDW bring findings together, check where they came from, compare like with like over time, and have a person review what to investigate next instead of relying on a mystery score.
fit: LDW's internal SEO research and review work.
Human reviewers who need to see where a website finding came from and how it compares with earlier evidence.
Internal validation of whether stronger evidence handling reduces recurring reconciliation and reporting work.
howItWorks: Replaceable sensors provide already-normalized or sanitized evidence into provider-specific adapters.
Tenant-scoped persistence preserves canonical observations, provenance, and compatible longitudinal snapshots.
Human-authored review history, measurements, and declared outcomes remain distinct from automated sensing.

Accepted internal workspace, service-run, portfolio, portability, external-review, measurement-interpretation, and SERP-validation surfaces remain decision-support only; provider retrieval and any production action stay separately authorized.
projects.maturity: An actively developed internal tool with a current synthetic Workbench for reviewing website and search evidence. The demo uses example data; it is not connected to a customer's live website or search accounts. There is no customer login, automatic website change, or standalone product release.

faqs.question: Can a customer buy G.A.S. Engine as standalone software?
faqs.answer: No. G.A.S. is LDW's internal SEO research tool. We use it to help our team review website and search findings; it is not software customers can buy or operate themselves.

faqs.question: Does G.A.S. automatically prioritize recommendations or change customer websites?
faqs.answer: No. A person reviews the findings and decides what to investigate. G.A.S. does not change a customer's website or promise a particular search ranking.

visuals.alt: Current G.A.S. Workbench synthetic review workspace showing website evidence and human review status
visuals.caption: Current Workbench synthetic demo. It uses example data to show how LDW reviews website and search findings; it is not connected to a customer's live accounts.

projects.homeSummary: LDW's custom-developed SEO research tool helps our team compare website findings over time, see where they came from, and explain what a person recommends looking at next.
projects.workWhy: The aim is to make an SEO review easier to follow: show what was found, where it came from, and why a person thinks it deserves a closer look.

projects.name: Document Control
projects.purpose: Explore structured document workflow, review, accountability, audit history, search, and export without claiming a completed customer deployment.
projects.description: A configurable LDW workflow application being developed service-first around controlled document lifecycle needs.
projects.boundary: Active development is not presented as a finished client engagement or mature standalone SaaS.
projects.whyItMatters: Controlled-document work becomes risky when reviewers cannot tell which version was approved, who acted, what changed, or how evidence can be exported. This project explores those problems with exact-version workflow evidence, auditability, portability, and explicit tenant boundaries.
fit: Teams that need structured review and approval around controlled documents or templates.
Organizations that care about exact-version evidence, audit history, role-aware workflow, and export.
Situations where a focused customer-owned augmentation may be preferable to replacing an existing document platform.
howItWorks: Documents and controlled templates keep immutable version identity and bounded change history.
Versioned workflows bind reviews and approvals to the exact document version and hash being acted on.
Tenant-aware roles, audit records, search/filtering, and export preserve accountability around the workflow.
The current product surface remains synthetic/test-only while production identity, uploads, scanning, recovery, and customer provisioning stay behind explicit readiness gates.
projects.maturity: Active development with substantial synthetic/test-only capability and accepted production-readiness foundations. It is not a production customer deployment and does not currently authorize live authentication, customer uploads, customer data, or production D1/R2 resources.

faqs.question: Is Document Control a finished DMS or eQMS that LDW is selling today?
faqs.answer: No. It is an active service-first product foundation being validated around controlled-document workflow needs. The current repository explicitly does not claim a production customer deployment.

faqs.question: Can customers upload real files or regulated data into it now?
faqs.answer: No. Current content-ingestion and product-surface work is staged with synthetic or non-sensitive test content. Production uploads, malware scanning, retention, recovery, identity, and customer provisioning require later explicit gates.

projects.cardBoundary: Active development · not a production customer deployment.

projects.name: Secure Exchange
projects.purpose: Develop a provider-neutral pattern for protected message and document exchange with clear queue ownership, retention, and accountability.
projects.description: Current foundation work uses a customer-owned isolated-deployment direction with an AWS-first reference architecture; production customer infrastructure is not yet provisioned.
evidence: Secure external intake and outbound workflow design
Individual workforce accountability and queue routing
Provider-neutral core with customer-owned deployment direction
projects.boundary: No public website claim implies that LDW currently operates production Secure Exchange infrastructure for customers.
projects.whyItMatters: Organizations often need to exchange sensitive messages or documents with people outside their normal systems without losing accountability for who may read, download, reply, file, complete, or dispose of an item. Secure Exchange is exploring that workflow without making transport state or a secure link stand in for application authorization.
fit: Organizations that need role-routed external message or document intake around an existing internal workflow.
Teams that need explicit evidence for opened, downloaded, filed/transferred, completed, and disposition states instead of treating them as the same event.
Customer-owned deployments where provider-specific services should remain adapters rather than become the business workflow itself.
howItWorks: Provider-neutral domain rules model threads, messages, attachments, queue routing, lifecycle, retention/disposition, and explicit access grants.
External bootstrap/session work is designed so possession of a browser session does not create wildcard application authority.
Synthetic commercial workflow slices validate intake, attachment review, staff-directed resolution, downstream filing simulation, completion, and disposition.
The current AWS-first direction remains a reference architecture for an isolated customer-owned deployment rather than a claim of live regulated production.
projects.maturity: Release 0.14 is a synthetic/local commercial-workflow demo. There is no production mail provider, Open Dental integration, customer data or PHI, production persistence, or regulated-production claim. A paying pilot or production deployment requires separate provider, BAA, support, ownership, security/privacy, and operational gates.

faqs.question: Is Secure Exchange already a production HIPAA-compliant service?
faqs.answer: No. The current product is synthetic/local validation work. Encryption, secure links, or cloud services by themselves do not establish HIPAA compliance, and any regulated deployment requires a separately reviewed end-to-end operating boundary.

faqs.question: Is the goal to replace a customer's existing systems?
faqs.answer: Not by default. The accepted direction is customer-owned augmentation: fit a secure exchange workflow around the customer's existing provider and operational process rather than requiring a standalone replacement.

projects.name: Owner Console
projects.purpose: Explore a clear home for an owner to see priorities and business updates in one place.
projects.description: Owner Console is an internal dashboard prototype for bringing day-to-day priorities and business updates together in a way an owner can scan quickly.
evidence: Clear views for priorities and business areas
projects.boundary: Fixture-only prototype using sample information. It is not connected to live business accounts, and it cannot perform business actions.
projects.whyItMatters: Small business owners often have to check several places to understand what needs attention. A single, readable dashboard can make the next step easier to spot.
fit: Owners who want a clearer view of current priorities.
Teams exploring how separate business updates could be organized in one place.
howItWorks: The prototype groups example updates into a home view and focused business areas.
All displayed information is synthetic sample data.
No accounts, providers, or business operations are connected.
projects.maturity: A fixture-only, non-production prototype. The current public-safe view uses synthetic information and does not connect to live business accounts.

faqs.question: Does Owner Console show live company information?
faqs.answer: No. The public example is a prototype with synthetic sample information and no live connections.

projects.homeSummary: An internal dashboard prototype for bringing an owner’s priorities and business updates together in one easy-to-scan place.
projects.workWhy: The idea is to make it easier to see what needs attention without checking a stack of separate tools.
projects.cardBoundary: Sample information only · no live accounts or actions.

projects.name: Reputation / MGR
projects.purpose: Explore a fair, simple way for small businesses to invite customers to leave honest reviews.
projects.description: Reputation / MGR is an active product-development effort exploring how a small business could make review follow-up clear and neutral, while using its existing business tools wherever they already do the job.
evidence: Product and service approach under development
Current research tracked in the project roadmap
projects.boundary: There is no working app or live customer service yet. Active development currently means product and service research; it does not mean a customer-ready tool, review sending, or connected accounts.
projects.whyItMatters: Owners need a straightforward way to ask customers for honest feedback without pressuring anyone or risking their standing with review sites.
fit: Small businesses considering a fair and consistent review follow-up process.
Businesses where existing scheduling, point-of-sale, or customer-management tools do not cover a demonstrated need.
howItWorks: The active work is evaluating what small businesses actually need and what their existing tools already provide.
The product direction rules out filtering customers based on whether they are likely to leave a positive review.
Any future software or customer service would require separate readiness and authorization.
projects.maturity: Active product and service development, currently focused on research and defining the right role for a review follow-up service. No functional runtime exists.

faqs.question: Can I use or buy this tool today?
faqs.answer: No. It is in active development at the research and product-definition stage; there is no working app or customer-ready service.

faqs.question: Does it help businesses filter for positive reviews?
faqs.answer: No. The product direction is neutral review requests and does not support review gating.

projects.homeSummary: Active development exploring a simple, fair way for small businesses to invite honest customer reviews. There is no working app yet.
projects.workWhy: The goal is a clear, neutral follow-up process that respects customer choice and review-site rules.
projects.cardBoundary: Active product research · no working app or customer service.

projects.name: Interview Facilitator
projects.purpose: Help a person run a consistent business or project discovery conversation and keep useful notes organized.
projects.description: Interview Facilitator is an internal workspace for preparing and guiding discovery interviews, capturing notes, and turning what a person learns into an organized follow-up.
projects.boundary: An internal development tool, not a public customer service. It is human-led and does not record conversations or make decisions about people.
projects.whyItMatters: A good discovery conversation helps an owner explain what is happening in their business. A guided workspace helps the interviewer listen consistently and keep the next steps straight.
fit: Human-led business and project discovery conversations.
Teams that want a repeatable way to prepare questions and organize follow-up notes.
howItWorks: The interviewer follows a structured conversation guide.
Notes and next steps stay organized for human review.
The tool does not record audio or autonomously assess a person.
projects.maturity: An active internal tool with an offline-first interview workflow and synthetic example content. It is not a CRM, recorder, chatbot, or automated qualification system.

faqs.question: Does it record or score the person being interviewed?
faqs.answer: No. It supports a human-led conversation and note organization; it does not record audio or make automated decisions about people.

projects.homeSummary: A guided workspace that helps a person prepare for discovery conversations, keep notes organized, and track follow-up.
projects.workWhy: It helps the interviewer stay present in the conversation and keep useful next steps from getting lost.
projects.cardBoundary: Internal development · human-led, with synthetic examples.
